A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tensor Decomposition Networks research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched, including the additional ablations and checklist in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original TDN prediction results on PubChemQCR, OC20, and OC22, together with runtime measurements and empirical approximation and equivariance errors.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds component ablations, NequIP integration experiments, an n-body rank sweep, and CPU/GPU efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.1 of v2 explicitly extend the proposed sharing mechanism to equivariant linear layers, beyond the CG-path sharing described in v1. The CP approximation and rank schedule remain unchanged. The newly documented removal of Equiformer's depth-wise tensor product does not itself establish when that implementation choice occurred.

E1.justification: v2 removes the OC20 S2EF 2M joint energy-and-force evaluation reported in v1 Section 4.4 and Table 3. It adds an n-body systems benchmark for downstream rank evaluation in Appendix D. PubChemQCR, PubChemQCR-S, and OC20/OC22 IS2RE coverage remain.

E2.justification: Removing the S2EF experiment removes its comparison against SchNet, DimeNet++, SpinConv, GemNet-OC, eSCN, and EquiformerV2. v2 adds paired component comparisons using TDN and NequIP in Table 5 and additional TDN variants in Table 8. Comparator membership in the retained PubChemQCR and IS2RE accuracy tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled component experiments, including a four-layer, width-64, L=2 TDN trained for 60 epochs, and an n-body rank-sweep protocol using three blocks, width 72, and 5000 epochs. CPU throughput testing is also added. Retained benchmark splits and training budgets remain stable. Table 1 changes energy units to meV/atom and resolves v1's conflicting force MAE/RMSE labels; these reporting corrections do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained tensor-level rank/error curves, v2 adds substantial analyses: accuracy and training-time ablations of CP and path sharing in TDN and NequIP (Table 5), downstream accuracy and equivariance sensitivity to rank on n-body systems (Table 7), and separate throughput/parameter ablations of CP, tensor-product sharing, and linear-layer sharing (Table 8).

E5.justification: Both versions average the original equivariance experiment over 1000 random rotations and report benchmark point estimates without training-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new checklist asserts that dataset sizes suffice for statistical significance, but introduces no statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The efficiency results are replaced: at L=3, Equiformer/TDN throughput changes from 48.4/142.9 samples/s in v1 Table 2 to 26.1/220.4 in v2 Table 4, with parameter counts changing from 33.43/4.42 to 54.7/4.5 million. Cross-version configurations are insufficiently matched to call this a same-setting gain. Tables 5, 7, and 8 add ablation outcomes, while the S2EF results disappear. Retained PubChemQCR and IS2RE numerical scores and Figures 2–3 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.2, their Appendix B proofs, and the arbitrary-order formulation in Appendix A retain the same mathematical content. The parameter-complexity notation changes from O(c^2 L^3) to O(c L^3) because c is redefined from multiplicity to per-path parameter count, rather than because a new bound is established.

C1.justification: The introduction softens v1's claim that the resulting layer maintains conventional tensor-product expressivity to having close expressive power. The central claims of approximate equivariance, universality at sufficient rank, reduced complexity, and a plug-and-play replacement remain. The expanded summary restates theoretical contributions already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 newly acknowledges a possible accuracy cost from path sharing and explains why ablated TDN still differs from vanilla Equiformer. It drops v1's account of larger Equiformer configurations failing to converge. Section 4.6 also introduces a mistaken interpretation: it attributes reduced training time to disabling the components, whereas Table 5 shows the reduction when they are enabled.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit public-code statement linking AIRS and substantially expands Appendix C with implementation sources, PyTorch Geometric adaptations, basis/cutoff choices, attention settings, and OC20/OC22 graph-construction parameters. New experiments include architecture, budget, and hardware details. These disclosures do not prove that existing experiments changed. Conversely, v1's explicit PubChemQCR TDN batch size of 32 is no longer stated.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Cormorant and Neural Relational Inference and removes the SpinConv and GemNet-OC references. Its introduction now distinguishes SO(2) and Gaunt approaches by their different expressivity, replacing v1's emphasis on remaining computational overhead. Most related-work discussion and research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Editing and reorganization are concentrated in experimental reporting: efficiency follows benchmark results, training paragraphs move into dataset-specific subsections, and limitations move from Appendix D to main Section 5. Appendix C is rewritten, affiliations are updated, and ablation/checklist sections are added. Most introductory, methodological, and theoretical prose retains its structure and wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds three ablation tables, removes the S2EF table, relocates retained tables, and expands the efficiency display with explicit speedup and parameter ratios. Table 1's metric headings and several captions are revised, including Figure 3's explanatory caption. Figures 1–3 retain identical graphics. The empirical displays change substantially beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence for the central accuracy–efficiency tradeoff through component controls, NequIP integration, and downstream rank sensitivity in Tables 5, 7, and 8. Expanded implementation documentation, code-access information, and the explicit accuracy limitation also improve reproducibility and claim calibration. These gains are partly offset by losing the OC20 catalyst force benchmark and introducing the training-time interpretation error in Section 4.6. On balance, the paper improves, but the evidence supports a limited overall gain.
